chunks: The whole group of them did not proceed on the same lines in such a way that we can know the height of their glory; but if it has to be done then it is the 'al-Mālik aḍ-ḍillīl' (the mislead king).

key_terms.الضِّلِيلُ: The misled or the one who leads others astray
key_terms.حَلْبَةٍ: A course of running or a path of praise/elevation
key_terms.قَصَبَتِهَا: Its head, leader, or foremost part

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'misled king' referred to in Imam Ali's view on the greatest poet?
ai.summary: In this concise evaluation, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the inconsistency of poets who praised the Umayyad caliphs, noting that their verses lacked a consistent standard of excellence. He identifies the 'misled king' (al-Malik al-Dillil), widely interpreted as Mu'awiya I, as the definitive subject of their praise, highlighting the political and spiritual deviation of the Umayyad rule from the true path.
